deep.reconstruction:
Nature of the page. This is not a worked derivation. It is a heavily corrected draft of a letter, with a short mathematical remark appended. It continues the previous page, which drafts 'Gegenbemerkungen zu den Bemerkungen des Herrn Hofrath Riemann' about the printing of a paper in Crelle's Journal (Borchardt is named there). That framing makes authorship and addressee uncertain; I flag it rather than resolve it.

Letter part (items listed as corrections to the printed paper):
- Item 1, previous page: in the second-order Taylor terms of a formula on 'S. 6 (S. 126)', the factor 1/2 was dropped.
- Item 2, this page: a proposal to denote the number of actually occurring simple branch points ('wirklich stattfindende einfache Verzweigungen') by a different letter, because the one first chosen is already used elsewhere. The cross-reference is 'S. 6, B. 127'.
- Then a request for help with the further printing and for speeding it up.
- Then a fragment of a personal letter ('Mein lieber ...! ... liebevolle Theilnahme für uns, die sich darin ausspricht, sehr gefreut').

Mathematical part ('Über die Form der algebraischen Function f mögen noch einige Bemerkungen folgen'):
- Setting: f lives on the Riemann surface of an algebraic relation F(s,z)=0. At finitely many points (pairs) (ε,ζ) it behaves like a fractional power of the local parameter, with rational exponents (the 'Grenzen').
- Step 1. Let n be the least common denominator of these exponents. Then f^n has integral exponents everywhere. Across the cross-cuts its factors become trivial, assuming the factors of f are n-th roots of unity; this is implicit, and the remark is mine.
- Step 2. Hence f^n is single-valued, i.e. a rational function R(s,z) on the surface, and f = R^(1/n).
- Step 3. R must be chosen so that at each pair (ε,ζ) where f is infinite it has a pole of order a multiple of n. Likewise every pair where it vanishes counts with multiplicity n.
- Step 4 (general case, factors not roots of unity). Take any function t with the same factors across the cross-cuts as f. Let x_μ, μ = 1..p, be auxiliary functions vanishing or with values at the relevant pairs (ε,ζ); this reading is uncertain. Then f·t/(x_1…x_p) is said to be rational in s, z and the parameters ε, ζ. Hence f = φ·t/(x_1 x_2 … x_p) with φ rational.
- This is the standard representation of a multiplicative (root or Prym-type) function as a fixed multiplicative function times a rational one.
errors: Step 2 needs the factors of f across the cross-cuts to be n-th roots of unity; otherwise f^n is not single-valued. The text only handles general factors later, via t.

If t has the same factors as f, it is f/t, not f·t, that is single-valued. As transcribed, 'f t/(x1…xp)' and 'f = φ t/(x1…xp)' are mutually inconsistent unless 't' means a reciprocal or the transcription is off. Possibly a slip or misreading.
The draft is fragmentary and the x_μ are undefined on the page, so the final formula cannot be checked fully.

results.what: Missing factor 1/2 in second-order terms of the two-variable Taylor expansion (an erratum to the printed paper)
A function with rational local exponents (lcm of denominators n) and root-of-unity factors is the n-th root of a rational function on the Riemann surface
results.modern_name: root functions / cyclic covers; sections of torsion line bundles

results.what: A multiplicative function equals a fixed function with the same multipliers times a rational function
results.modern_name: multiplicative (Prym) functions; quotient of two sections of a flat line bundle is meromorphic

deep.surprise_reason: The page is mainly a letter draft about printing corrections. Its mathematical remark is standard material on root and multiplicative functions, already in Riemann's circle. Authorship of the draft is itself unclear.

checkable.asserts: The second-order Taylor coefficient carries 1/2: the coefficient of x**2 in exp(x+2y) is 1/2, so this expression should be 0.
With exponents 1/3 and -1/2 (lcm n=6), f**6 is rational, so this should be 0.

transcription_corrections: 'Grenzen ε und ζ' / 'Grenzenpaare (ε, ζ)' is probably 'Exponenten' for the first word, with (ε,ζ) denoting points (value pairs) of the surface; uncertain.
'f t/(x1 x2 ... xp)' may be 'f/t' or involve t^{-1}; the image is ambiguous.
Header 'siehe S. 6. B 127' probably refers to page 127 of the printed paper (with S. 126 on the previous page).
